tokens.name: --surface-fill
tokens.note: the TINTED pane fill. Unset by default; read as var(--surface-fill, <1.4 fill>) — hsl(var(--glass-tint) / var(--card-opacity)) on the tinted pane, / .58 under frost, / var(--glass-opacity) in base.css, / .97 on the tip and menu, / .65 on the menubar list, / 1 on the phone notebook. The tier sets it on <body> (it reads --glass-tint, so it must resolve there)

tokens.name: --surface-filter
tokens.note: the blur, wherever the house draws one: unset by default, read as var(--surface-filter, var(--frost-filter)) on frost panes and the disconnected body, var(--surface-filter, var(--frost-filter) brightness(1.03) saturate(1.03)) on the frost bar-chip (the WHOLE chain is the fallback), and over the three literal blurs (#graphTip, #notebook, #menubar .mb-list). Off is the whole value none, never blur(0). The base.css .glass filter still reads --glass-filter (the TINTED filter) (1.4 fallback name: --frost-filter)

tokens.name: --surface-edge
tokens.note: the pane edge colour; unset by default, read as var(--surface-edge, var(--glass-border-color)) on panes, islands and the tip, over --glass-hairline on .mb-list and over the notebook's literal edge (1.4 fallback name: --glass-border-color)

tokens.name: --surface-edge-width
tokens.note: the pane edge width; unset by default, read as var(--surface-edge-width, var(--glass-border)), or over 1px on the menus and notebook (1.4 fallback name: --glass-border)

tokens.name: --surface-shadow
tokens.note: height 2 of 4, a pane: unset by default, read as var(--surface-shadow, var(--glass-shadow)) on .dev, .glass and the islands, and over the badge's literal 0 4px 12px. LITE: one layer falling down; FLAT: 0 0 0 0 transparent. Its value must one day drop 1.4's upward term (INTENT L01) (1.4 fallback name: --glass-shadow)

tokens.name: --surface-shadow-docked
tokens.note: height 1 of 4: a docked card in the rack

tokens.name: --surface-shadow-float

LITE: one layer; FLAT: 0 0 0 0 transparent

tokens.name: --surface-shadow-menu
tokens.note: height 4 of 4, menus, tips and popovers: declared in skin.css, read as var(--surface-shadow-menu, var(--glass-shadow)) on #graphTip, the menubar list, the value tooltip .k-val (INTENT O4 default), the ⓘ panel and the control hint. LITE: one layer; FLAT: 0 0 0 0 transparent

tokens.name: --surface-sheen

tokens.name: --surface-veil
tokens.note: the REFRACTIVE pane fill: unset by default, read as var(--surface-veil, transparent) and, under frost, var(--surface-veil, hsl(0 0% 0% / .10)) dark / hsl(0 0% 100% / .10) light on the disconnected body; the notebook reads it over transparent. LITE gives it the tinted fill so an unblurred pane stays legible

tokens.name: --surface-lift
tokens.note: the disconnected bar-chip's NON-BLUR backdrop (brightness(1.03) saturate(1.03)) with frost off: unset by default, read as var(--surface-lift, brightness(1.03) saturate(1.03)). Not the blur and not the pane, so it is its own switch; LITE sets it to none (F1 §4.1: a render surface per head)

tokens.name: --relief-raise
tokens.note: PRESS ME: unset by default, read as var(--relief-raise, var(--neu-raise)) on the knob puck, the trigger and the chosen segment (that last one is INTENT L33). FLAT: 0 0 0 0 transparent (1.4 fallback name: --neu-raise)

tokens.name: --relief-well

FLAT: 0 0 0 0 transparent (1.4 fallback name: --neu-inset)

tokens.name: --state-hover

tokens.name: --state-on
tokens.note: ON and CHOSEN: the frost face, never an accent fill. Declared in skin.css; read as var(--state-on, var(--glass-raise)) on .sw.on, .trig.on, .seg-b.on and by the window rail chip (--chip-on). The dark value is the rail chip’s §56 frost, so the two draw ON alike

tokens.name: --state-on-light

tokens.name: --state-press

tokens.name: --state-press-scale

tokens.name: --state-focus
tokens.note: keyboard focus: an OUTLINE shorthand (2px solid accent A), drawn outside with outline-offset 2px on :focus-visible; undeclared (it reads the accent), read as var(--state-focus, 2px solid var(--acc)). tokens.name: --light-angle
tokens.note: LIGHT ANGLE: where the one light is, clockwise from straight up (0 above, 315 upper left); written on <html> by the GUI window; the relief, the cast and the shine turn with it (docs/THEMES.md)

tokens.name: --light-sin
tokens.note: sin() of LIGHT ANGLE, for the offsets

tokens.name: --light-cos
tokens.note: cos() of LIGHT ANGLE, for the offsets

tokens.name: --shadow-amount
tokens.note: SHADOW 0–2: the cast's strength (BASINS' ABOUT shadow at this amount); read under html[data-cast]

tokens.name: --shadow-dist
tokens.note: DISTANCE: how far the pane shadow falls from the light (×1, ×3, ×5 for the three heights); the shine uses it too

tokens.name: --shadow-soft
tokens.note: SOFTNESS: the pane shadow's blur (×1, ×2.25, ×3.5 for the three heights)

tokens.name: --shine-amount
tokens.note: SHINE 0–1: the shadow's opposite, a white light toward LIGHT ANGLE, blended additively on rack cards; read under html[data-shine]

tokens.name: --shine-term
tokens.note: the shine as one shadow layer (declared on html[data-shine] body from the four numbers above); a rack card draws it on its ::before, other panes in their shadow list

tokens.name: --cast-pane
tokens.note: the cast at pane height (html[data-cast] body): BASINS' ABOUT shadow turned by LIGHT ANGLE; it becomes --surface-shadow

tokens.name: --cast-float
tokens.note: the cast at floating-window height; it becomes --surface-shadow-float

tokens.name: --cast-menu
tokens.note: the cast at menu height; it becomes --surface-shadow-menu

tokens.name: --solid-pane
tokens.note: CARD STYLE · SOLID: the opaque pane, in the glass tint (body[data-card="solid"])

tokens.name: --solid-lit
tokens.note: SOLID's relief toward the light: a lighter mix of the pane

tokens.name: --solid-shade
tokens.note: SOLID's relief away from the light: a darker mix of the pane

tokens.name: --faces-transition-source
tokens.note: CONTROL FACES · BLEND: the crossing layer's colour (BASINS material.css) (not skin-settable: its alpha is a runtime number, which no token type describes)

tokens.name: --faces-transition-mode
tokens.note: CONTROL FACES · BLEND: the crossing layer's blend (burn dark, dodge light)

tokens.name: --faces-solid-pct
tokens.note: CONTROL FACES · BLEND: how much of the solid face is left, (1 − BLEND)·100 %, written on <body> by the GUI window

tokens.name: --faces-transition-alpha
tokens.note: CONTROL FACES · BLEND: the crossing layer's alpha, .22·sin(π·BLEND), written on <body>

tokens.name: --pane-edge
tokens.note: EDGE: a window pane's rim (cards, kit windows, the islands, the notebook, the modulation panes), read before --surface-edge; menus and popovers keep theirs (BASINS draws no window edge)

tokens.name: --rack-gap
tokens.note: SPACING: the gap between rack windows: 0 · 3 · 6 · 16 px (0, TIGHT, DEFAULT, AIRY; BASINS' levels and AIRY); 1.4: 10 px

tokens.name: --rack-inset
tokens.note: SPACING: the rack's distance from the screen's edge: 0 · 3 · 6 · 16 px; 1.4: 10 px

tokens.name: --pane-pad
tokens.note: SPACING: the padding inside a pane around its controls: 6 · 6 · 8 · 9 px, never under 6 (1.4: 7 · 7 · 10 px)

tokens.name: --rail-gap
tokens.note: SPACING: the gap between the chips of a docked chip rail, 0 · 2 · 4 · 6 px, written on <html> by the GUI window (gui.js); read as var(--rail-gap, var(--rail-gap-derived)), so the written value wins and a page with no GUI window gets the derived one

tokens.name: --rack-flush-radius
tokens.note: SPACING at 0 (html[data-flush]): a rack window's corner in the flush slab

tokens.name: --rack-flush-shadow
tokens.note: SPACING at 0: no pane shadow or shine inside the flush slab

tokens.name: --solid-lift
tokens.note: SOLID: how far the highlight mixes toward white, ΔL/(100 − L) with ΔL = 8 + 20·(1 − L/100) (core/look.js solidRelief); fallback 18 % dark, 70 % light

tokens.name: --solid-sink
tokens.note: SOLID: how far the shade mixes toward black, ΔL/L with ΔL = 6 + 14·L/100; fallback 32 % dark, 22 % light

tokens.name: --shine-gain
tokens.note: the shine's strength by the pane's lightness, 1 + 1.2·(1 − L/100): a dark pane shines more

tokens.name: --m2-focus-ring
tokens.note: the plugin's focus ring as an OUTLINE (read after --state-focus, which a skin may set)

tokens.name: --m2-power-seat

tokens.name: --info-over-fade
